You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: every wrong submission costs 1 and every demo request costs 1. An
instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt cap is reached, and
reaching the cap is charged the full cap. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

How to work, in every instance (follow this exactly): keep a program library in the folder /home/ubuntu/continual-arc-baselines/.workbench/runs/adhoc-openclawlearner-1790687857/attempts/d3ae97d7f78548fbbe6aa9202f4eeb9d/system/state/workspace/programs, one Python file per task, named for its task id (/home/ubuntu/continual-arc-baselines/.workbench/runs/adhoc-openclawlearner-1790687857/attempts/d3ae97d7f78548fbbe6aa9202f4eeb9d/system/state/workspace/programs/<task id>.py), defining transform(grid), which takes an input grid as a list of lists of integers and returns the output grid.
1. When an instance starts, look for the task's file. If it exists, run its transform on the test input and submit the result before anything else.
2. If there is no file, or its answer was wrong, request demonstration pairs as you judge necessary, write or fix transform, and run it on every pair you have received until it reproduces all of them; then submit its output for the test input. Checking a program on the pairs is free.
3. Submit only grids that your program produced.
4. After the verdict, save the program that reproduced all the pairs to the task's file, replacing any older version, then finish.

---
name: continual-arc
description: Solve Continual-ARC task instances with persistent per-task Python transforms, demos, and verified submissions.
---

# Continual ARC

For Continual-ARC instances that provide a task id, test grid, demonstrations, and a persistent program library:

1. At instance start, inspect `programs/<task id>.py`. If it exists, run its `transform(test_grid)` and submit that exact result before any other task action, as required by the instance protocol.
2. If the file is absent or its first submission is judged incorrect, inspect all examples as whole grids before requesting more. Locate separators and panels, then infer the operation from demo input-output dimensions, colors, and positions—not from a plausible-looking relationship between colors alone. Keep candidate transforms provisional until they reproduce every pair. Request a demo only when it can discriminate between concrete candidate rules; after each pair, test candidates against all examples. An incorrect verdict rejects the tested rule: return to the examples and revise the program before another submission, rather than changing colors, dimensions, or outputs speculatively.
3. Implement `transform(grid)` only when the rule is supported, then run it on every demonstrated input. Compare full grids, including dimensions, colors, and unchanged cells. Before submitting, validate the exact transform result is a nonempty rectangular grid with 1–30 rows and columns and integer cells 0–9; build the action grid from that result. Submit only after the program reproduces every available pair. If the demo cap arrives without a rule that reproduces the pairs, retain the uncertainty and make at most one evidence-based, validated attempt within the limit.
4. On every instance turn, follow its response protocol exactly: one action per turn and exactly one action JSON object on the final line. Never hand-construct a submission independently of the executed transform.
5. After a correct verdict, ensure the reproduced transform is saved at `programs/<task id>.py`, then finish the instance. Do not describe or save an unverified transform as validated; preserve an existing useful implementation unless a new one reproduces all available demos.

def transform(grid):
    # The full-width 8 rows mark boundaries. Recolor the leftmost 8-column
    # guide and boundary rows to 2, preserving all other cells.
    return [[2 if (c == 0 or all(v == 8 for v in row)) and value == 8 else value
             for c, value in enumerate(row)] for row in grid]
PY
